newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila firms seek price cut on Canadian wheat.
newsitem.headline: Manila firms seek price cut on Canadian wheat.

text.p: Philippine firms have asked suppliers of Canadian wheat to reduce prices on orders contracted for deliveries this month due to supply delays, officials at local flour millers and Manila grains traders said on Thursday.

"Our supplier of Canadian spring wheat told us he could not meet the agreed delivery date due to weather problems. We agreed for a later delivery as long as there is just compensation such as price reduction," an executive at a Philippine mill which bought Canadian wheat told Reuters.
The executive said Philippine firms bought less than 25,000 tonnes of Canadian wheat for delivery this month and early March.
Grains traders however said they have heard rumours that between 60,000 and 100,000 tonnes of Canadian wheat bought by Philippine firms early this month for prompt shipment have been delayed.
Philippine firms have now shifted back to the U.S. wheat market because of the transportation problem in Canada, a local trader said.
